source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Immediate: treatment and transport are time-critical because a life threat may be reversible.","B":"Minor: the person can walk or has injuries that can safely wait for later care.","C":"Delayed: serious injury is present, but treatment can wait while immediate patients are managed.","D":"Expectant/deceased: available resources are not directed first when immediate patients can be saved."}}
source_row.rationale: In the HHS CHEMM START algorithm, red means Immediate: the person needs time-critical intervention and transport to survive. Green is minor, yellow is delayed, and black is expectant/deceased. Option A is correct.
source_row.source_detail: START Adult Triage Algorithm: Red = Immediate; the person can be helped by immediate intervention/transport and needs medical attention within minutes for survival, including airway, breathing, or circulation compromise. HHS CHEMM current web publication of the Benson-modified START algorithm; CHEMM background identifies the 1996 modification; page/version currentness rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN 2026 prioritization/Management of Care check completed first.
